We need to determine number of C=O groups in the compound. We have no SMILES given. We need to get IR spectra maybe to see carbonyl stretch. Or carbon NMR? But easiest is to get IR spectra which shows C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. However we need count. Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). But we need to know the compound. No structure provided. We must request measurement? The sample at hand is presumably some unknown compound. We can use IR spectra to detect carbonyl peaks. But counting may be ambiguous if overlapping. Could also use carbon NMR to count carbonyl carbons. That may be more precise. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool. That returns a string with peaks and assignments? Probably just list of chemical shifts. Carbonyl carbons appear around 190-210 ppm (ketones, aldehydes) or 160-180 for esters, amides. So we can count peaks in that region.

Thus we should call carbon_nmr_spectra.
